newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn sees 2.4 bln DM from '97 Lufthansa sale.
newsitem.headline: Bonn sees 2.4 bln DM from '97 Lufthansa sale.

text.p: The German Transportation and Transport Ministry said on Monday the government would receive as much as 2.4 billion marks this year when the remaining 35.7 percent stake in airlines Lufthansa AG is sold to the public.

Bonn transferred the shares to state development agency Kreditanstalt fuer Wiederaufbau (KfW) last year and received 2.1 billion marks that was budgeted in 1996. The KfW expects to get around 4.5 billion marks for the shares and the difference, 2.4 billion, would go to Bonn and be budgeted in 1997.

The ministry gave more details about the expected sale after issuing a statement about changes to German law that take effect on July 1 and ensure that a majority of Lufthansa remains in the hands of Germans.
"Now nothing stands in the way of the Lufthansa privatisation and sale of shares on the stock market," said Transport Minister Matthias Wissmann in a statement.
"Because this law among other things creates the conditions to sell the government's Lufthansa shares on the stock exchange."
The sale of the shares is one of several big privatisations the government hopes to complete this year in order to raise funds in its bid to qualify for European economic and monetary union.

Until now, it was not clear whether the government would float the additional Lufthansa shares or sell them in some other way to private investors. The government is expected to float the shares in the autumn.

Lufthansa shareholders last week approved measures, which include giving Lufthansa the right to buy shares if the percentage of foreign ownership rises above 40 percent, were expected to be given shareholder approval.
Lufthansa, which has only one major German shareholder with a 10 percent stake, must remain in majority control by Germans to guarantee the country's bilateral flight agreements.
